title: The Expiration Date Is a Suggestion
editorialNotes: 43% is the 2025 Food Date Label Survey figure (gtm.json date-label-lie), the only number allowed hero treatment. Other survey percentages stay body copy.

thread.element: date label sticker peeling off the pack

copy.headline: The date on your food is not regulated by the federal government.
44% of Americans think the government oversees food date labels.
items: The only federally mandated date label in the U.S. is on infant formula.
Everything else is the manufacturer's best guess at peak quality.
copy.citation: 2025 Food Date Label Survey — Harvard Law, ReFED, Johns Hopkins, via Harris Poll

copy.headline: "Best by" = quality, not safety.
items: "Sell by" = stock rotation for the store, not a warning for you.
"Use by" = the closest thing to a safety date, and even that one confused 49% of people surveyed.

copy.heroNumberCaption: 43% of consumers say they always or usually throw food away based on the date label alone. Up from 37% in 2016. The confusion is getting worse, not better.

copy.headline: Gen Z and millennials are the worst offenders:
items: 52% and 51% always or usually toss food at the label date.

copy.headline: Manufacturers benefit from you throwing food out early.
copy.body: Earlier disposal = faster repurchase cycle. The dates aren't designed to protect you. They're designed to sell more product.

copy.headline: The sniff test is more reliable than the printed date for most refrigerated foods.
items: Your nose evolved over millions of years.
The label was printed last Tuesday.

copy.headline: Stop trusting the sticker. Start trusting the food.
